title: Anchor benchmark and perturbation suite for embedding accuracy and rerank stability
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: build a reproducible, extensible evaluation harness for embedding accuracy and reranker stability that covers: representative anchor sets (human-labeled and weak-supervised), synthetic perturbations (typos, paraphrases, entity swaps), rerank offline simulation, and drift-sensitive alerts. This ticket delivers: 1) an "anchor set" generator pipeline and storage layout (S3 + manifest), 2) a perturbation library to create controlled degradation tests, 3) an offline reranking simulator that measures MRR, Recall@k, NDCG, pairwise cosine gap, and calibration metrics across model variants and quantization profiles, and 4) perf/scaling tests for embeddings endpoint (latency percentiles and throughput by batch size) integrated with CI and Grafana dashboards.

Success criteria: - Baseline anchor sets covering 5 domains (support KB, docs, product descriptions, short queries, conversational turns). - Perturbation suite supports 6 types with configurable intensity. - CI job that runs nightly on canary models and emits metric deltas + alerts when MRR drops >2% or cosine gap widens >0.05. - Dashboard with historical trends and a rerunable job spec for reproducing any regression locally. - End-to-end run time for evaluation pipeline under 2 hours for a 10k-query anchor set on a single mGPU node.

Architecture notes: - Data ingestion: ingest sampling jobs from existing user query logs (anonymized) and curated human labels from Drive (confluence link below). - Storage: S3 prefix with versioned manifests (anchor-v{YYYYMMDD}), small metadata CSVs for quick lookups. - Orchestration: Airflow DAG + k8s job template for heavy rerank simulation. - Metrics: push all metrics via Prometheus-exporter bridge; alert rules in Grafana/Prometheus. - Reproducibility: store RNG seeds, perturbation parameters and model git tag per run.

Trade-offs considered: - Human labeling coverage vs cost: we will start with smaller high-quality anchors (2k examples) and extend via weak supervision. - Heavy-weight rerank sim gives better fidelity but costs compute; schedule nightly runs and keep a lightweight quick-check that samples fewer examples for on-change PR checks. - We considered using existing embedding-eval harness but it lacked perturbation primitives and rerank sim, so we are building a thin compatibility layer instead of forking.

Data & privacy: logging uses anonymized query IDs only; no PII. We will coordinate with Security for storage lifecycle and retention policies.
comments: 2026-02-28 Maya Patel: Initial triage and scope. Decided to prioritize five domains and a synthetic perturbation API. Added as P1 due to upcoming Dedicated SLA review.
2026-03-03 Ethan Brooks: Design review completed. Agreed on metrics (MRR, Recall@k, NDCG, cosine gap, calibration curves). Airflow DAG sketch uploaded to Confluence.
2026-03-06 Data team (Liam Chen): Completed anonymized sampling job for 50k candidate queries; stored preliminary 10k seed set to s3. Link in attachments.

2026-03-09 Engineering: Implemented perturbation library (typo/char-drop, paraphrase via paraphrase-microservice, entity-swap using slot map). Unit tests added. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/412

2026-03-11 Ethan Brooks: Ran first offline rerank simulation across three candidate models (open-7b, quant-7b, redwood-7b). Observations: MRR delta -3.1% for quant-7b on paraphrase-heavy set; cosine gap increased by 0.07. Captured raw outputs in s3 for inspection.

2026-03-12 Maya Patel: Performance profiling for embeddings endpoint: batch=1 p95=45ms, batch=8 p95=70ms; throughput saturated at batch=32 on single A10 with 420 req/s for 512-d vectors. Need follow-up ENG ticket to evaluate KV cache interaction for small sequences.
2026-03-13 PM review (Olivia Grant): Approved moving to canary nightly runs; requested alert thresholds be conservative for first two weeks.
2026-03-14 Security (Priya Rao): Reviewed data retention and encryption; OK with S3 lifecycle 90d and KMS key scoping. No additional review required for initial rollout.

notes: Related internal artifacts: design doc at Confluence (see attachments), benchmark runner code in /benchmarks, evaluation results snapshots in s3.
We intentionally model paraphrase and entity-preservation stress cases to catch regressions that simple recall metrics miss.
This harness will later be extended to support embeddings for multi-vector representations and cross-encoder rerankers as separate modules.
